Every week, a client calls me with the same question: do we need to stop using artificial intelligence until the new law is ready? My answer is no. Nobody is going to rule out AI in business. But you need to carry out a simple review now. First, find out where you use automated decisions, for example in credit or in hiring. Second, check if a person can look into a decision when a customer complains. And third, draw up a short internal policy. The watchdogs are not waiting for the new law, so neither should you.

I am not against regulation, but I am worried about how it is being drawn up. Lawmakers spend three years writing a law, and in those three years the technology changes completely. When the rules are finally phased in, they describe systems that nobody uses anymore. My suggestion is simple. Instead of long lists of prohibited technologies, set out clear principles, and let the agencies update the details every year. If the law cannot keep up with the technology, at least the regulator can.
